sections.normalized_html:
To apply a transformation to the graph of a function, we modify its equation according to the direction of the shift:

  • A horizontal shift left by [MATH: 3] units means we replace every [MATH: x] in the original function with [MATH: (x + 3).]

  • A vertical shift up by [MATH: 2] units means we add [MATH: 2] to the entire function.

We start with the function: [MATH: r(x) = \dfrac{a - 5}{x} + 7]

To shift left [MATH: 3] units, we replace [MATH: x] with [MATH: x + 3{:}] [MATH: \dfrac{a - 5}{x + 3} + 7]

Then, to shift up [MATH: 2] units, we add [MATH: 2] to the whole expression: [MATH: \left(\dfrac{a - 5}{x + 3} + 7\right) + 2]

Therefore, by simplifying, we find the equation that defines [MATH: s] is [MATH: s(x)|= ((a − 5)/(x + 3) + 7) + 2; = (a − 5)/(x + 3) + 9.]

So, the equation of [MATH: r(x)] becomes [MATH: r(x) = \dfrac{a}{x + 3}.]

Now, to identify the value of [MATH: a,] we choose a convenient point on the graph. For example, when [MATH: x = -2,] the graph passes through [MATH: y = 6.] Plugging [MATH: (-2, 6)] into [MATH: r(x),] we get [MATH: r(x)|= (a)/(x + 3); 6|= (a)/(− 2 + 3); 6|= (a)/(1); a|= 6.]

Thus, the equation of [MATH: r(x)] is [MATH: r(x) = \dfrac{6}{x + 3}.]

Therefore, to find an expression for [MATH: s(x),] we replace each [MATH: x] in [MATH: r(x)] by [MATH: (x+2)] and simplify: [MATH: s(x)|= r(x + 2); = (6)/((x + 2) + 3); = (6)/(x + 5).]

Item 2 — Example: Evaluating a Rational Function

The function [MATH: g] is defined by [MATH: g(x) = \dfrac{x^{2} - 4x + 2}{x - 2}.] What is the value of [MATH: g(-2)?]

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Explanation:

Therefore, the value of [MATH: g(-2)] is [MATH: -\dfrac{7}{2}.]
